discovered_risks: Third-party menu-bar managers can hide or temporarily omit a valid status item independently of Disk Steward.
The earlier automatic-termination diagnosis was not supported once the live process, status-item smoke report, and iBar state were inspected together.

evidence: The notarized /Applications/Disk Steward.app passed codesign --verify --deep --strict, Gatekeeper assessment, and Scripts/Distribution/verify-release.
A LaunchServices launch created Disk Steward process 90344, then the process disappeared without a crash report.
Unified logging recorded AppKit AutomaticTermination setting _kLSApplicationWouldBeTerminatedByTALKey=1 immediately before the menu-bar-only process disappeared.
Sources/DiskStewardApp/ApplicationDelegate.swift creates the status controller but does not hold a ProcessInfo automatic-termination activity or explicitly disable automatic termination.
codesign reported the installed application valid on disk and satisfying its designated requirement.
spctl accepted the installed application with source Notarized Developer ID.
Scripts/Distribution/verify-release passed the exact /Applications bundle.

last_audit.recommended_action: Reopen TASK-210, keep a process-lifetime automatic-termination assertion for the menu-bar monitor, add regression coverage, rebuild, and prove a Finder or LaunchServices launch remains alive with a visible status item.

Restarting iBar Pro and relaunching Disk Steward restored the icon without changing Disk Steward code, configuration, or data.
